name: Alice Springs Telegraph Station
reason: Rule 1-3: the town's founding site; Wikivoyage See listing, heritage buildings, exhibits and waterhole walks, hours 8AM-9PM; multi-hour visit.
objection: Close to town and Wikipedia-light, but a clear headline heritage stop.

name: Anzac Hill
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage-listed town lookout over Alice Springs and the MacDonnell Ranges, free, open access.
objection: Short stop and one source; but the town's signature viewpoint and sunset spot.

name: Olive Pink Botanic Garden
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage lists this free desert botanic garden with trails (8AM-6PM); an hour's walk.
objection: A garden that 'doesn't bloom much' per the guide; one source.

name: Alice Springs Reptile Centre
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage See listing, paid walk-through of local reptiles and a saltwater croc; open to public.
objection: One source and a small attraction (about an hour); a commercial centre rather than a landmark.

name: Alice Springs School of the Air
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage names it ('Famous!') and it runs visitor tours, but it shares one complex with the RFDS base listed as a single Wikivoyage entry.
objection: For: separate tour and famous outback institution (2310 views). Against: near-duplicate of the RFDS complex entry, which the guide treats as one place.

name: Royal Flying Doctor Service Alice Springs Base
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage names the RFDS base with School of the Air as 'Famous!'; visitor tour, museum and cafe, open to public.
objection: One source and the complex also holds School of the Air; kept as the single entry for the complex.

name: Old Timer's Museum
reason: Rule 1: one Wikivoyage listing ('worth a visit') for a pioneer/camel-train museum at a retirement village; I could not confirm current public opening.
objection: For: guide recommends it, outback pioneer collection. Against: one dated source, 0 views, sits inside an aged-care village and no current hours found.

name: Women's Museum of Australia
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage and Tourism NT list the Women's Museum in the Old Alice Springs Gaol (gaol buildings open to walk through).
objection: Hours and prices conflict between listings; a niche museum.

name: The Residency
reason: Rule 1-2: one Wikivoyage listing, museum house, volunteer-run with limited hours.
objection: For: 1927 heritage house open inside as a museum. Against: single source, small and limited opening, a 30-minute visit at best.

name: Araluen Cultural Precinct
reason: Rule 1-3: two counted sources (Wikivoyage, Tourism NT); galleries and Namatjira works, the town's arts precinct.
objection: Its museum is closed for refurbishment per the museum's site; galleries still open, confirm in research.

name: Museum of Central Australia
reason: Rule 2/3: the museum's own site says it is closed to the public until further notice (refurbishment), and it is part of the Araluen Cultural Precinct kept as one spot.
objection: Wikivoyage describes a good fossil and wildlife museum; could be re-added if it reopens.

name: Adelaide House
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage 'well worth a visit' first stone building on Todd Mall, open with communications displays and tea; half-hour stop.
objection: Tiny volunteer-run museum, one source.

name: National Road Transport Museum
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage lists the Road Transport Hall of Fame and the Old Ghan museum next door; paid, an hour or more.
objection: One source; a niche trucks museum south of town.

name: Central Australian Aviation Museum
reason: Rule 1: one Wikivoyage mention ('a number of older planes') beside the School of the Air.
objection: For: open aircraft collection with a town-reliant-on-aviation story. Against: single source, a short visit, shares the RFDS/School of the Air complex.

name: Strehlow Research Centre
reason: Rule 1-2: no visitor-oriented source; Wikipedia only, and the Museum of Central Australia that houses it is closed to the public, access by researcher appointment only.
objection: Was once open for Aboriginal culture displays; the closure makes it fail rule 2 now.

name: Stuart Town Gaol
reason: Rule 1-2: Tourism NT and the National Trust list it, but it is open only limited weekday hours with keys collected from Hartley Street School and a closed summer.
objection: For: Alice's oldest surviving building, Tourism NT page. Against: access is by key deposit, tiny, short visit.

name: Hartley Street School
reason: Rule 1-2: Tourism NT and Discover Central Australia list it as a National Trust museum (School of the Air's first broadcast studio); hours Mon-Fri only.
objection: For: genuine museum, free to enter with $5 ticket. Against: no counted source in the candidate list, small, 30 minutes.

name: Todd Mall
reason: Rule 2/3: a pedestrian shopping street; its draws (Adelaide House, markets) are covered separately.
objection: Wikivoyage places the town's heart here and it has 3915 views, but a street of shops is not a stop in itself.

name: Alice Springs Markets (Todd Mall and Heavitree Gap)
reason: Rule 4: markets run only alternate Sundays.
objection: None; a recurring weekly-or-less event.

name: Heavitree Gap
reason: Rule 1-3: described in Wikivoyage's geography text only, not as a stop; a gap the highway passes through.
objection: 3270 views and Arrernte sacred site, but no visitor source sends anyone to stop there.

name: Honeymoon Gap
reason: Rule 1/3: Wikivoyage names it as a turnoff on the Bullen Road loop; Nature Park with a waterhole and picnic area.
objection: For: a named scenic gap with swimming/waterhole and Larapinta Trail access. Against: single source that is only a turnoff mention, minor next to Simpsons Gap and Standley Chasm.

name: Pioneer Park Racecourse
reason: Rule 4: a race-meeting venue, an event not a permanent attraction.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it, but only race days draw visitors.

name: Camels Australia
reason: Rule 1-2 (operator): a camel farm operator, but a distinct visitable place stands behind it, the farm at Stuart Wells with an enclosure visit and an art/souvenir shop (Wikivoyage).
objection: For: Wikivoyage describes a walk-in farm visit, not just a tour. Against: it is a commercial operator, 0 views, one source.

name: Pyndan Camel Tracks
reason: Operator: one-hour or half-day camel treks; no distinct place stands behind it other than the Ilparpa Valley itself.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it as the only camel-riding experience based in Alice Springs, but it is an activity not a place.

name: Original Glen Helen Homestead
reason: Rule 3: the historic homestead sits at the Glen Helen resort at the end of the sealed road, a part of the Glen Helen spot already kept.
objection: Tourism NT lists it; but it is part of the Glen Helen resort and gorge stop.

name: Ellery Creek Big Hole
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage and Tourism NT both name this permanent waterhole for swimming and camping; a headline West Macs stop.
objection: Cold water and a sealed-road drive; no real objection.

name: Serpentine Gorge
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage and Tourism NT name it, with a walk to a lookout/pool.
objection: Smaller than Ormiston and Ellery; the walk is short.

name: Serpentine Chalet Dam
reason: Rule 2/3: ruins reached only by 4WD, a minor ruin beside a bush camp.
objection: Tourism NT names it as an attraction; but a ruin with little to do.

name: Ormiston Gorge
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage and Tourism NT name this gorge and pound with permanent waterhole and walks; headline of the West Macs.
objection: None of substance.

name: Redbank Gorge
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage and Tourism NT name it, the chasm at the base of Mount Sonder.
objection: Rough access (the last stretch is rough, 4WD recommended); but still a named, accessible gorge.

name: Roma Gorge
reason: Rule 1-3: single Wikivoyage mention on a permit-only 4WD track; remote rock-art site seen by very few.
objection: Has rock art; but no visitor source gives access or a reason, rarely visited.

name: Jay Creek Waterhole
reason: Rule 1: Tourism NT names it as a permanent waterhole beside the Larapinta Trail.
objection: For: a named permanent waterhole in a national park. Against: one source, on the Larapinta Trail rather than a destination of its own, little reason to stop.

name: Birthday Waterhole
reason: Rule 1-3: only Tourism NT's list; a semi-permanent pool on the Hugh River on a remote 4WD track.
objection: Named on the board's page; but remote and rarely visited, no description of anything to do.

name: Owen Springs Reserve
reason: Rule 2/3: a quiet 4WD bush-camping reserve; Tourism NT's page frames it as camping, not a thing to see.
objection: Has ruins and creek country; but the draw is camping and it is rarely visited.

name: Wallaby Gap
reason: Rule 3: a creek bed and intermediate campsite on the Larapinta Trail, part of the trail.
objection: Tourism NT names it; but it is a trail section, not a destination.

name: Kalarranga Lookout
reason: Rule 1/3: Tourism NT names the sandstone-staircase lookout in Finke Gorge National Park, which is itself a walk within Palm Valley.
objection: For: a named lookout with a panorama (I opened the Tourism NT Finke Gorge page). Against: part of the Palm Valley park walks, one source.

name: Palm Valley
reason: Rule 1-3: Tourism NT and Wikivoyage name this oasis of rare red cabbage palms with swimming and walks; 2412 views.
objection: High-clearance 4WD or tour only; but a genuine headline of Finke Gorge National Park.

name: Illamurta Springs Conservation Reserve
reason: Rule 1-3: a remote reserve on a 4WD route with a camp; one Tourism NT mention with no description of anything to see.
objection: Springs and ruins exist; but very rarely visited.

name: Wallace Rockhole
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage names the Aboriginal community with cultural tours and camping, via a 4WD side track.
objection: For: a guided cultural experience. Against: single source, visits need booking and community access, short sealed-road reach is disputed.

name: Ewaninga Conservation Reserve
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage's Red Centre and Chambers Pillar pages both list the Ewaninga rock carvings, free, short walk.
objection: A half-hour roadside stop with weathered carvings.

name: Rainbow Valley
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage's Red Centre page lists the striped sandstone cliffs with a short walk; known sunset spot.
objection: Dirt access last stretch, 4WD advised.

name: Henbury Meteorites Conservation Reserve
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage's Alice Springs page lists twelve craters with short walks; 6949 views.
objection: Remote, but a distinctive natural feature.

name: Curtin Springs
reason: Rule 1-3: two Wikivoyage pages (Red Centre, Uluru) name this cattle station and roadhouse on the road to Uluru, with walks and paper-making.
objection: Mostly a roadhouse and campground, so the draw is the station experience.

name: Gosses Bluff (Tnorala)
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage names the meteorite crater and sacred site with picnic tables and walks; 10365 views.
objection: Access is by permit/loop road and only a lookout, but a significant landmark.

name: Ross River Homestead
reason: Rule 2: a resort and accommodation base; the draw is the eastern gorges which are separate spots.
objection: Historic homestead; but accommodation, not an attraction.

name: Emily Gap
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage lists Emily Gap twice (MacDonnell Ranges, Alice Springs); sacred Arrernte site with rock paintings, free.
objection: Short stop, but the most visited East Macs gap.

name: Jessie Gap
reason: Rule 1/3: one Wikivoyage mention as a quick stop on the Ross Highway.
objection: For: named gap with picnic area. Against: single source, a ten-minute roadside look, close to Emily Gap.

name: Corroboree Rock
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage names it, a sacred rock formation with a short walk around it.
objection: A small formation, half-hour stop.

name: John Hayes Rock Hole
reason: Rule 3: a roadside rockhole named in a list only, with nothing described to do.
objection: 0 views, one bare mention.

name: Trephina Gorge Nature Park
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage names the gorge with river red gums, walks and camping; an East Macs highlight.
objection: One source; but a clear day-trip draw.

name: Ruby Gap Nature Park
reason: Rule 1/2: one Wikivoyage mention of a 4WD-only park with a gorge and ruby-rush history.
objection: For: scenic remote gorge, 963 views. Against: 4WD-only, one source, rarely visited.

name: N'Dhala Gorge Nature Park
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage names the gorge with Aboriginal rock art and a walk.
objection: 4WD or dirt track; one source.

name: Arltunga Historical Reserve
reason: Rule 1-3: two Wikivoyage pages list the gold-mining ghost town with interpretive centre and old buildings.
objection: Dirt access, remote; but a well-known historic reserve.

name: Uluru Base Walk
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage lists the 9.8 km walk around Uluru, 3-4 hours.
objection: Overlaps with Mala/Kuniya/Liru sections, but the base walk is the main experience.

name: Mala Walk
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage lists this 2 km walk from the Mala car park to Kantju Gorge, with ranger talks.
objection: Section of the base walk; but listed and signed as a walk of its own.

name: Kuniya Walk
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage lists this 1 km walk to Mutitjulu Waterhole with rock art.
objection: Part of the base circuit; the waterhole is a distinct destination.

name: Liru Walk
reason: Rule 3: a connector path between the Cultural Centre and the base of Uluru, a section of the same area as the other Uluru walks.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it as a walk (4 km, 1.5 hours); but it is mainly an access path with no distinct reason to go.

name: Valley of the Winds Walk
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage calls it 'truly magnificent and should not be missed': 7.4 km into Kata Tjuta.
objection: Closed in hot weather; still a headline walk.

name: Walpa Gorge Walk
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage lists the easy 2.6 km walk into Kata Tjuta's gorge.
objection: Overlaps with Kata Tjuta, but a separate walk.

name: Kata Tjuta Dune Viewing Area
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage lists the 600 m dune walk with views of Kata Tjuta and Uluru, allow 30 minutes.
objection: Short stop, one source.

name: Talinguru Nyakunytjaku
reason: Rule 1-3: Parks Australia's Uluru site lists it as the main sunrise viewing area with platforms and a 1.4 km walk circuit.
objection: Overlaps with Uluru's viewing but a distinct place.

name: Uluru-Kata Tjuta Cultural Centre
reason: Rule 1-3: two counted sources (Wikivoyage, Parks Australia) list the cultural centre with Anangu art and exhibits; open daily.
objection: Visitor centre, but a recognised culture stop.

name: Tjukurpa Tunnel
reason: Rule 3: an exhibit inside the Cultural Centre, part of that spot.
objection: Parks Australia names it; but not a separate stop.

name: Field of Light
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage lists Bruce Munro's permanent installation; 3431 views.
objection: Tours and timing needed; but permanent and a major Uluru draw.

name: Imalung Lookout
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage lists the central dune lookout with Uluru views, free.
objection: Overlaps with other Yulara dune lookouts; kept as the one representative.

name: Pioneer Lookout
reason: Rule 3: near-duplicate of Imalung Lookout in the same Yulara resort, a dune lookout over Uluru.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it separately; but not a distinct draw.

name: Naninga Lookout
reason: Rule 3: near-duplicate of Imalung Lookout in Yulara; more distant views.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it separately; but not a distinct draw.

name: Gallery of Central Australia
reason: Rule 2: a commercial gallery selling Indigenous art in the resort, effectively a shop.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it, and it shows Central Desert art; but it is a retail gallery.

name: Sounds of Silence Dinner
reason: Operator/event: a booked evening dinner by coach; no distinct place stands behind it (a desert dining dune area, not a named spot).
objection: Wikivoyage calls it extremely popular; but it is an operator product.

name: Kings Canyon Rim Walk
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage calls it the 'star trail' of Watarrka, a 7 km loop.
objection: Overlaps with Kings Canyon spot; but a signature walk.

name: Garden of Eden (Kings Canyon)
reason: Rule 3: a waterhole on the Rim Walk, part of that walk.
objection: Wikivoyage names it; but a side stop on the Rim Walk.

name: King Creek Walk
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage lists the short, wheelchair-accessible canyon-floor walk with panels.
objection: Overlaps with Kings Canyon; but the easy alternative.

name: Giles Track
reason: Rule 1/3: one Wikivoyage listing of a 22 km track to Kathleen Springs; a multi-day-ish walk requiring registration.
objection: For: a named long walk, which the rules include. Against: one source, not otherwise promoted, mostly a link between two kept walks.

name: Kathleen Springs Walk
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage says 'a lot of people miss this - don't!'; short flat accessible walk.
objection: One source.

name: Mount Ebenezer Roadhouse
reason: Rule 2: a roadhouse with basic accommodation; the art room is a side feature.
objection: Wikivoyage suggests an Aboriginal-culture stay; but a roadhouse is a shop and lodging.
